html.label: INTRO
html.b: Hello. Thank you for taking this survey about the election and issues facing your community.

title.b: Are you registered to vote?
People have many reasons for voting or not voting. Did you vote in the recent midterm elections, held on November 3, 2026?
What state or territory do you live in now?

radio.label: Q_REGION
radio.title: State Region Punching
radio.row: Northeast: Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island, New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey
Midwest: Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri

South: West Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, Virginia, District of Columbia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Kentucky, Tennessee, Mississippi, Alabama, Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana
West: Montana, Idaho, Wyoming, Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, Nevada, Alaska, Washington, Oregon, California, Hawaii

title.b: What is your current ZIP Code?
What is your age?

html.label: Main_Intro
html.b: First, you will see a few questions about the 2026 midterm elections.

radio.label: Q1

title.b: Which candidate did you vote for in the 2026 election for the U.S. House of Representatives?

radio.row: I did not vote in that race

radio.label: Q2

title.b: Was your vote for the U.S. House of Representatives primarily in support of your preferred candidate or in opposition to the other candidate?

radio.row: Mostly in support of my preferred candidate
Mostly in opposition to the other candidate

radio.label: Q3

title.b: Which candidate did you vote for in the 2026 election for U.S. Senate?

radio.row: I did not vote in that race

radio.label: Q4
radio.cond: hQ3.r1 and (Q3.r1 or Q3.r2 or Q3.r3)

title.b: Was your vote for U.S. Senate primarily in support of your preferred candidate or in opposition to the other candidate?

radio.row: Mostly in support of my preferred candidate
Mostly in opposition to the other candidate

radio.label: Q5

title.b: Which candidate did you vote for in the 2026 election for Governor?

radio.row: I did not vote in that race

radio.label: Q6
radio.cond: hQ5.r1 and (Q5.r1 or Q5.r2 or Q5.r3)

title.b: Was your vote for Governor primarily in support of your preferred candidate or in opposition to the other candidate?

radio.row: Mostly in support of my preferred candidate
Mostly in opposition to the other candidate

radio.label: QNEW
radio.title: Thinking about your vote in this year’s election, was your vote more about supporting Donald Trump, opposing Donald Trump or did Donald Trump not have much impact on how you voted?
radio.row: Donald Trump did not have much impact on how I voted'

radio.label: Q7

title.b: How much did each source influence your vote decision?

radio.row: Political groups that run campaigns to educate and persuade voters

title.b: Which word best describes how you feel about the election outcome?

html.label: Intro_Q9
html.b: Next, we’re going to focus on some specific issues related to the 2026 midterms.

title.b: Which of the following issues were most important in deciding your vote?

radio.label: hQ10
radio.title: Hidden to select hQ10 quota

title.b: Which specific [pipe:hQ10] issues had the greatest influence on your vote?
Thinking about the November 2026 elections, how much, if at all, did candidates’ positions toward each of the following affect which candidate you voted for?
Which ONE of the following industries, if any, had the greatest impact on how you voted in the November 2026 elections?

html.label: Intro_Q13
html.b: The next set of questions you will see focuses specifically on health care and the recent midterm elections.

title.b: Of all the issues that you considered when deciding to vote, how much of a factor were health care issues? When you give your response, please give it in terms of a percent, so if you had 100 points to allocate to indicate how important health care issues were to you, how many points would you give it? Obviously, the higher the number, the more important it was to you.

checkbox.label: Q14

title.b: Which of the following health care issues were the most important in deciding your vote?

checkbox.comment: Please select up to two issues.
checkbox.row: Out-of-pocket costs not covered by your insurance, such as copays and deductibles
Transparency and fraud in health care spending
Restoring the cuts to ACA/Obamacare insurance subsidies
Attacks on science in health care policy
Addressing racial disparities in health care and outcomes
Vaccine requirements and recommendations, such as for children or schools
Protecting Medicare for current and future seniors
Changes to Medicaid eligibility and funding
Delays and denials from your insurance company

radio.label: Q15

title.b: How important was health care affordability in deciding your vote in the 2026 midterm elections?

radio.row: A major factor, but not the most important

title.b: During the 2026 campaign cycle, how often did you hear candidates or campaigns talk about lowering health care costs?

checkbox.label: Q17

title.b: Which affordability issue related to health care do you remember hearing candidates or campaigns talk about most often?

checkbox.row: General cost of living or inflation
I do not remember hearing about any of these

radio.label: Q18

title.b: How much, if anything, did you hear candidates or campaigns talk about:

radio.row: Insurance companies delaying or denying patients the care they need
Transparency and fraud in the health care system

title.b: How believable did you find candidates’ messages about lowering health care costs?
How believable did you find candidates’ messages about lowering prescription drug costs?
How believable did you find candidates’ messages about lowering health insurance premiums?
Which party did you think had the stronger message on lowering health care costs during the campaign?
Which party did you think had the stronger message on lowering prescription drug costs during the campaign?
Which party did you think had the stronger message on lowering health insurance premiums during the campaign?
How confident are you that the newly elected Congress will make health care more affordable?
And how confident are you that the newly elected Congress will make prescription medicines more affordable?
Compared with before the election, are you now more optimistic, less optimistic, or do you feel about the same when it comes to health care affordability and prescription medicine costs?

Thinking more specifically about drug costs, how much, if anything, did you hear candidates or campaigns talk about basing what Americans pay for prescription medicines on the prices paid in other countries, also known as “Most Favored Nation” or MFN pricing?
How much, if anything, did you hear candidates or campaigns talk about Medicaid funding cuts or removing people from the Medicaid program?
How much, if anything, did you hear candidates or campaigns talk about reductions in or restoring Affordable Care Act (ACA)/Obamacare premium subsidies?

radio.label: Q30

title.b: Please indicate how much each of the following issues influenced your decision about how to vote in the 2026 midterm elections.

radio.row: Most Favored Nation (MFN) pricing for prescription medicines
Medicaid funding cuts/removing people from Medicaid
Reductions in ACA/Obamacare insurance premium subsidies
The Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement

title.b: Through the course of the 2026 election, has your view of health insurance companies become more favorable, less favorable, or stayed about the same?
And, through the course of the 2026 election, has your view of pharmaceutical companies become more favorable, less favorable, or stayed about the same?

radio.label: Q33

title.b: Looking ahead after the elections, please indicate whether you agree or disagree with each of the following statements.

radio.row: Maintaining U.S. leadership in medicine development and innovation should be a priority for the newly elected Congress.
Policymakers should prioritize biotechnology when competing economically with China over the next two years.

title.b: Looking back, how much did vaccine policy affect your 2026 vote?
Do you know what President Trump’s policy on vaccines is?
Do you support or oppose President Trump’s policy on vaccines?
How concerned are you that political pressure has influenced vaccine recommendations?

html.label: Q36Intro
html.b: Finally, here are a few questions about health care beyond the midterms.

title.b: Who should be held most accountable if health care costs do not improve over the next two years?

radio.label: hQ37
radio.title: Hidden to get a SAMPLE

title.b: Do you expect to see major progress on addressing health care issues in the new Congress that will return in January 2027 to begin a new legislative session?
Do you want to see major progress on addressing health care issues in the new Congress that will return in January 2027 to begin a new legislative session?

html.label: DIntro
html.b: Lastly, here are a few questions for background purposes. Your answers will remain confidential.

radio.label: D2

title.b: Do you currently take any prescription medications?

radio.row: Yes, only occasionally or as needed

title.b: How often, if at all, do you currently take prescription medication(s)?

radio.label: D4

title.b: Are you currently covered by any form of health insurance, or do you not have health insurance at this time?

radio.row: I am covered by health insurance
I am not covered by health insurance

title.b: In general, would you say your health is…
What is your current marital status?
Are you the parent or guardian of one or more children under the age of 18?
Do you consider yourself a member of the following movements?

radio.label: D10

title.b: Are you or anyone in your household currently or have ever been a member of a labor union?

radio.row: Yes, in the past but not currently

html.label: END
html.b: That concludes our survey. Thank you for taking the time to share your views.
